newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Shell kills two Singapore soldiers in NZ exercise.
newsitem.headline: Shell kills two Singapore soldiers in NZ exercise.

text.p: Two Singaporean soldiers were killed and 12 soldiers injured on Sunday when an artillery shell exploded prematurely during a training exercise in New Zealand, an army spokesman said.
It was the second fatal accident in just over two weeks involving Singaporean soldiers at the central North Island army training base of Waiouru.
Eleven of the injured in Sunday's explosion were Singaporeans and one a New Zealander, who was slightly hurt.
"There was an accident at a Singapore gun position. The Singaporeans sustained 13 casualties including two fatalities," New Zealand army spokesman Major Steven French told Reuters.
"It would appear a shell exploded prematurely."
He said the injured were being ferried by four helicopters to nearby hospitals. The injuries ranged from serious to light, French said, adding that he could give no more details.
A witness told Radio New Zealand that it appeared that a field gun had exploded.
The Singapore soldiers, from the 23rd artillery battalion, arrived in New Zealand in early February and are due to return in April. The battalion was involved in a live firing exercise at the time.
Singapore soldiers commonly train in New Zealand because of the shortage of facilities and space at home.
Last month one Singapore soldier was killed and another seriously injured after their Land Rover rolled and crashed in an accident at the Waiouru camp.
